required_behaviors: git.branch git.worktree and git.commit require distinct host-owned capabilities
host-approved approval_ref is required by default before intent
git.branch binds current repository HEAD and branch absence
git.worktree binds branch revision and target absence
git.commit binds expected HEAD and an observed selected-path snapshot
git.commit is restricted to an isolated linked worktree
repository worktree paths and Git metadata remain inside the canonical workspace boundary
linked worktrees are isolated outside the source worktree
hooks system/global config recursive submodules and inherited GIT environment overrides are disabled or bounded
configured clean smudge or process filters fail closed before checkout or add
per-surface leases and fencing tokens are revalidated before mutation
intent receipt is emitted before the first repository side effect
git.commit commits only declared paths through a temporary index and compare-and-swap ref update while preserving unrelated staged state
host-owned Git identity is required for commit creation
deadlines bound every Git subprocess and cancel before unstarted mutations
ambiguous outcomes are reconciled to succeeded failed or uncertain without blind retry
completion receipts chain to the exact intent receipt
branch worktree commit fixture produces one verifiable task receipt chain
